body.statement:
Determine whether there is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\) and every unequal-clique design in the model class,
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)
 \ge c\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}.
\]
The lower bound must hold when the infimum defining \(\mathcal R_\alpha\) ranges over every measurable interval procedure, including procedures randomized by the independent external randomizer \(R\).  This universal linear lower bound is the sole residual question.
body.justification: The capped optimizer, trimming dual, unrestricted upper bound, no-cap formula, and exact consistency boundary are proved; this question is retained solely for the matching all-measurable randomized-interval lower bound.
body.gap: Only the universal linear relation \(\mathcal R_\alpha\gtrsim\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\) remains open; the optimizer, duality, upper bound, and zero-versus-nonzero boundary are no longer part of the gap.
body.consumer: Closing this question would add a two-sided sharp expected-length rate without changing the already-proved consistency boundary.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove a universal constant lower bound of linear order in the capped water-filling modulus for every measurable interval procedure, including procedures using the independent external randomizer.
obligation.obstruction: The proved capped perturbation and common-location no-reveal construction yield a cubic lower bound, but they do not establish the posterior interval spread or concentration-function control needed for a linear lower bound under heterogeneous moving-support erasures.
obligation.attempted: The KKT optimizer, strengthened trimming dual, no-cap identity, factor-five unrestricted upper bound, and cubic all-procedure converse have been completed. Per the maximality directive, the rejected posterior-spread construction was not retried or generalized.
obligation.partial_result:
The capped optimizer and both computable sides are closed.  The strengthened trimming duality gives
\[
 \omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q)
 \le\frac52\omega_\alpha(w,q),
 \qquad
 \omega_1(w,q)\le\rho_0(w,q)\le2\omega_1(w,q).
\]
Together with the trimmed interval, \(\mathrm{thm{:}capped\text{-}modulus\text{-}upper}\) proves
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)
 \le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}.
\]
When no cap binds, the active quadratic constraint gives
\(\omega_\alpha(w,q)=\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\).  On the converse side, \(\mathrm{lem{:}capped\text{-}erasure\text{-}consistency\text{-}lower}\) proves
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)
 \ge
 \frac{\omega_\alpha(w,q)^3}
 {128\log(1/\alpha)+8\omega_\alpha(w,q)^2}
 \ge
 \frac{\omega_\alpha(w,q)^3}{136\log(1/\alpha)}.
\]
Thus the only unresolved step is to replace this cubic converse by a universal linear converse at nonzero finite confidence.
